notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already used up, so no search was run. Every page was opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py, each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed): the nine campaign sites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (learned from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step, python -m ballot.local_sites files, was run), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, and the University of Minnesota's election archive. No search engine was read in place of the search tool, and the real databases were not written.
No birth year is recorded for anyone. The election archive shows birth dates on two pages, but its source is a birth index, so neither was taken.

Mike Slavik: the election archive has a person of the same name from another county who ran for another office around 2002. Nothing on that page ties him to the Dakota County commissioner, so nothing was taken from it.

Republican endorsements: none could be recorded for Cherie Johnson, Dawn Gillman or Natalie Barnes; no local party unit's page naming them was found without a search. Dawn Gillman's site calls her "a trusted conservative", which is not a party or endorsement statement, so no own_words is recorded for her; no site read carries an explicit party or endorsement statement by the candidate.
Kari Rehrauer's own site lists Coon Rapids City Council 2020-2024; she is a sitting legislator with a record page, so it is not recorded here.

Not read, nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (robots.txt asks scripts to stay out), so nothing is recorded for Luis A. Bartolomei or Heather Pipenhagen; Clearwater County's site (robots.txt likewise), so nothing for Karin R. Hughes; Pope County's site (its pages are empty without scripts), so nothing for Paul Wildman; Pine City Public Schools' board page was not found (James Foster).

The official pages read show that these candidates do not hold the office sought today: Kanabec County lists Wendy Caswell for District 3 (Kevin Troupe) and Morrison County lists Robert Kasper for District 4 (Deb Gruber). The Otsego council page, the Hermantown, Brooklyn Center and Rochester council pages, the Willmar school board page and the West St. Paul-Mendota Heights-Eagan board page were looked through for David Shaptala, Candi Mock, Gretchen Enger, LaMar Hicks, Forrest Rice and Dwight H Larson without a match.

Nothing citable was found for eleven candidates, who are listed with no findings: Kevin Troupe, Deb Gruber, Paul Wildman, Karin R. Hughes, Candi Mock, David Shaptala, Dwight H Larson, Forrest Rice, James Foster, Luis A. Bartolomei and Heather Pipenhagen.

For the second reader: www.gillmanforhouse.com/about answered 525 once; the home page answered. Lincoln County's commissioners page and Kanabec County's board page print commissioners' addresses and phone numbers beside their names, and Sauk Rapids-Rice's board page prints an address; none of that was kept.
verifier_notes: Every url in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent; all 24 pages answered on the first try and each states what is recorded. 36 findings checked, 36 kept, none removed.

Wording corrected in seven places: the two DFL endorsement lines (the party's page prints no year); Dawn Gillman's site (the headings are in capitals, and the line reads "17B"); Gretchen Enger's site (her family name is in the address, not on the page); the election archive line for Natalie Barnes (cut to the race, the party and the place; her occupation dropped); Lincoln County's page for Mic VanDeVere (the town printed beside his name dropped); LaMar Hicks's site (office filed for added).

The nine campaign sites were checked against the name, office and website cells of the Secretary of State's filing files John saved; each is the address that candidate filed for this race. No other cell of those files was read out.
Dan Johnson (ISD 47): on the district's page each member's "Term Expires" line follows the member's name; the line after "Director: Dan Johnson" reads 12/31/2026.
Pete Weismann: the line after "Pete Weismann Clerk" reads "Elected on January 1, 2023 Expires 12/31/26".
Nothing from the never-collected list is in any field. Several official pages print phone numbers or addresses beside the names; none is kept here.
